source.title: Cefazolin Dialytic Clearance by High-Efficiency and High-Flux Hemodialyzers

source_integrity_notes: The Results section reports P = 0.4517 for systemic clearance in nonoliguric versus remaining high-efficiency subjects, while the Discussion reports P = 0.34 for the same 3.32 versus 2.79 mL/min comparison. The discrepancy was retained and not corrected.
The appended erratum corrects parameter-designation errors in equations 1 and 2 of the pharmacokinetic model description.
schema_gaps: The model has no dedicated field for standard deviation. SD values from Table 4 are retained in original_result_text rather than encoded as confidence intervals.
The model has no dedicated erratum atom kind. The equation correction is represented as atom_kind=other with an erratum tag.
extraction_limitations: The study enrolled 25 uninfected hemodialysis patients and assessed pharmacokinetics rather than clinical infection outcomes.

Dialyzer group assignment was site-dependent rather than randomized, and the high-efficiency group used multiple dialyzer types across two sites while the high-flux group used cellulose triacetate dialyzers at one site.
Dialytic clearance was estimated indirectly from a pharmacokinetic model rather than measured by direct dialysate or paired arterial-venous methods.
Dosing recommendations rely on population simulations and an 8 mg/L susceptibility breakpoint used by the 2001 source. Current clinical use requires separate verification.
All model-extracted atoms remain needs_review because no independent human reviewer step is represented.
